layers.note: A low, mat-forming sedge that dominates snowbeds and the wettest, latest-melting meadow hollows.

moisture.note: Wet to moist ground under a late snowpack.

elevation_m.note: Low in Alaska; subalpine to alpine further south.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −15 to 0 °C; gone below −25 °C and above 4 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −40 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −48 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 5 to 14 °C; gone below 3 °C, where summers are too short, and above 17 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 400 to 2,300 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 200.

degree_days_5.note: About 80 to 1,000 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 30.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.5, gone by 0.35.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Black alpine sedge grows from Alaska and Yukon through British Columbia and the Cascades to the Sierra Nevada, and east through the Rockies to Colorado (general range knowledge; not checked against PLANTS). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
